observation: Actual full durable original PNG opened at original resolution once in this author invocation before the continuation summary; this inventory reuses that observation, not an old review or modern figure.
sourceFacts: One tall qualitative liquid surface-layer molecular-force schematic, with exactly five hollow circles numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 down one vertical line.
The successive center gaps visibly decrease downwards: gap12 > gap23 > gap34 > gap45. The hand-drawn distances are not measured molecular coordinates or readings.
Molecule 1 has two solid force arrows: F_2 upward from its top, and F_3,4,5 downward from its bottom. Their tails touch the corresponding molecule boundary.

Molecule 2 has three solid force arrows: F_3 upward from its top; F_1 downward from its lower-left boundary; F_4,5,6 downward from its lower-right boundary. The two downward arrows are separate and unequal drawn lengths.
No force arrows are drawn on molecules 3, 4, 5. No axis, scale, tick, velocity, net-force arrow or calibrated magnitude is printed.
All five force arrows are solid, not dashed. Their directions express the source attraction/repulsion relationships, not measured force magnitudes.

Horizontal segmented liquid texture spans the background; lines are more closely spaced near the upper surface. The uppermost horizontal line identifies the upper liquid boundary; no calibration or exact molecular-row count is assigned to the texture.
The printed grouped force labels visibly list 3,4,5 and 4,5,6 without a visible ellipsis; the source prose expands them with ellipsis as sums over the remaining deeper molecules.
